question.text: Under the 'DIY (Do-it-Yourself)' organisational model for SIA described in Chapter 7.2.4, the SE develops its OWN impact-assessment tools. Which characteristic does DIY share with the FULLY INTEGRATED model?

answer.text: Both require the SE to engage an external SRO-empanelled agency
Both share similar benefits and drawbacks (customisation advantage, but resource-intensive to develop and less comparable across SEs)
Both are prohibited for SSE-listed SEs
Both are free of cost to implement

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7.2.4 states: 'This model [DIY] is similar to integrated Social Impact Assessment in terms of its benefits and drawbacks.' Both give customisation but require financial + technical resource to build and may suffer comparability issues with other SEs. The Trap: A describes the Outsourcing Model. C is false — SSE-listed SEs can use internal models so long as they are assured by an empanelled SIA. D is obviously wrong. Cross-Exam Context: The build-vs-buy trade-off mirrors in-house vs outsourced compliance decisions tested in III-A/III-C. Assessor's Pro-Tip: If the SE has adopted DIY or Integrated, your assurance procedures must add a 'tool-validation' step: verify that the DIY tool maps to at least one SAS standard. Un-mapped DIY indicators are not assurable.
